thread:
maria (PM): Quick sync — Pilot readiness for the Optimize toolkit (batching + caching + quant recs + eval-triggered alerts). Customer asks keep coming: canary gating, per-route SLOs, and clear rollback criteria. Need a proposed MVP cut and launch gating.

devon (eng): For MVP I'd push batching suggestions + KV prefix caching heuristics. Those are low-risk and give clear econ wins. Quant recs are higher risk because they require model-variant validation.

ben (ml eng): Agreed. Quant recommendations need a validation loop: offline metrics + a small online compare. Not ready for wide rollout in week 1.

rhea (data ops): Eval-alerts are high-value for customers but they need stable eval sets. Do we have 3 canonical eval sets per pilot customer?

maria (PM): We have 2 customers with eval sets; ask #3 in progress. Proposal: MVP = batching + caching + basic quant guidance (opt-in docs only) + eval-alerting as alpha (email + console flags).

samir (solutions): Customers will ask for gating knobs. Launch criteria we should commit to:
- clear canary plan (1% -> 10% over 24h) with automatic rollback on regression
- per-route latency p95 under 150ms for hosted pilot or regression policy
- econ signal: >=8% token-cost reduction on standard prompt suite
- eval alert precision >= 80% for small regression signals

devon (eng): Canary config in code would look like:```yaml
canary:
  traffic: [1,10]
  interval: 24h
  rollback_on: [eval_regression, latency_p95_increase]
```
We can wire that into the rollout service.

ben (ml eng): For eval regression detection, propose a quick metric set: answer-F1, perplexity-delta, and a quality-score model. Thresholds should be adjustable per-customer.

rhea (data ops): Operational checklist for MVP:
- onboarding guide for eval sets + schema
- demo dashboards for alert triage
- playbook: how to interpret alerts + remediate

maria (PM): Scope negotiation notes: drop auto-quant-tuning for MVP, include deterministic docs + quant tradeoff table. Post-MVP: auto-suggest quant profiles + A/B online validation.

samir (solutions): Customers will want SLA language. For pilot, offer SLOs in writing but not SLA credits.

devon (eng): Implementation estimate: batching heuristics + caching = 3 sprints, canary + rollout hooks = 1 sprint, eval-alert plumbing + dashboard = 2 sprints. We can parallelize across two squads.

maria (PM): Action items:
- @devon: break down tasks and PRD updates (due EOD Thu)
- @ben: spec eval metrics + initial thresholds (due Mon)
- @rhea: reach out to cust #3 to finalize eval set (ASAP)
- @samir: draft pilot customer comms with canary playbook (due Tue)
- @deploy-bot: create ticket OPT-431 and link: https://linear.app/REDWOOD/issue/OPT-431

samir (solutions): +1 on comms. Also suggest a short FAQ for pilots explaining why quant auto-tune is not included in MVP.

ben (ml eng): One more tradeoff: if we include aggressive batching by default we might push tail latency for some routes. Need per-route opt-out.

devon (eng): We'll add per-route batching controls and a global safety cap.

rhea (data ops): If eval-alerting goes live, include a daily digest and a critical-channel Slack hook for severity=high.

maria (PM): Cool. I'll update the PRD with these gating criteria and scope cuts. If anyone has objections to the MVP scope (drop auto-quant-tuning, include alpha alerts), speak now. :eyes: :thumbsup:

samir (solutions): :thumbsup:

devon (eng): :thumbsup:

ben (ml eng): slight concern but fine for pilot.

rhea (data ops): go for it.

deploy-bot: Ticket OPT-431 created and assigned to devon. Link: https://linear.app/REDWOOD/issue/OPT-431

maria (PM): Thanks team — will post updated PRD link shortly.
